rob_tool_version: JBI critical appraisal checklist for studies reporting prevalence data, 9 items (Munn et al.)
signalling_responses: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
rationale: Coverage of the identified sample is incomplete and the shortfall is partly undocumented. Only 420 of the 515 eligible patients (81.6%) completed 3-year follow-up, and completers differed from non-completers on two prognostically relevant variables (shorter DUP, lower baseline SOFAS; both p < 0.05), with no imputation or weighting. In addition the employment denominator itself does not match the analysed subgroup: the printed 30.0% for the schizophrenia subgroup is arithmetically impossible on n = 374 and implies a base of 370, so about four patients are silently absent from the employment analysis.

bias_direction: unclear: differential attrition on baseline functioning, and an undocumented shortfall in the employment denominator, could move the proportion in either direction

rob_tool_version: JBI critical appraisal checklist for studies reporting prevalence data, 9 items (Munn et al.)
signalling_responses: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition?
rationale: Psychosis was identified by ICD-10 criteria, with the final research diagnosis ascertained at 3 years from the longitudinal course using outpatient and inpatient records and the computerised clinical database, under a written protocol with weekly consensus meetings and inter-rater ICCs of 0.70 to 1.00 for DUP and the major outcome measures. Diagnosis is clinical rather than by structured research interview, which is a limitation, but the criteria and the ascertainment process are stated.

rob_tool_version: JBI critical appraisal checklist for studies reporting prevalence data, 9 items (Munn et al.)
signalling_responses: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
rationale: Employment was determined for every month of the 3 years from records using standardised data-entry forms, which is standard across participants; but WHAT was counted cannot be established, because the source defines the same variable in two incompatible ways (Methods 2.2 includes full-time study, Table 1 footnote b and Table 2 footnote e count work only). Ascertainment is also entirely from clinical records, with no direct enquiry of the participant and no validated vocational measure, and the report itself concedes that 'only data that could be reliably extracted from records were targeted for retrieval and analysis'.
source_location: chang2016, Methods 2.2 Measures, p. 2; Table 1 footnote b and Table 2 footnote e, p. 3
bias_direction: towards overestimate if full-time students are inside the numerator, since the construct would then be paid work or education rather than paid work
